searchText: yea i'm not sold on the benefits of eip-4444 -- and if 4444 is accepted, calldata pricing should come down to reflect that it is no longer permanently stored and in any case, my point is that code can still be stored in a separate (cheaper) database because it a) cannot be constructed dynamically and b) can't be updated IIRC some alternative designs were discussed, but in the end the reasoning was that the intrinsic cost of initcodes (same as calldata) itself is enough to cover this (much larger than hashing cost).
